title.narrative: Integrated health and Nutrition service in Afgoye district, Lower Shabelle Region Somalia

description.narrative: ltpgtAYUUB proposes a 12-month integrated health and nutrition response in rural Afgooye District, one of the priority districts under the SHF Reserve Allocation, where prolonged drought, displacement, and overstretched health systems have sharply reduced access to essential services. The project will restore and strengthen life-saving care for children under five, pregnant and lactating women, and other vulnerable households, directly contributing to reduced preventable morbidity and mortality while reinforcing community resilience.ltbrgtThe project will be implemented through a network of fixed and outreach platforms, including 2 health facilities and 2 outreach sites, complemented by primary health units and referral linkages targeting Mareerey Fixed MCH/OTP ,Muuri Fixed/OTP and 2 Outreach Sites (Aanoole,Sabiib,Baalguri, Mordile,Sagaalaad, Tawakal),Through these platforms, AYUUB will reach approximately 25,000 people with essential health services and treat 3,500 children for acute malnutrition. Services will include outpatient and mental health consultations, antenatal and postnatal care, skilled deliveries, emergency obstetric referrals, routine immunization, and integrated management of acute malnutrition. Health and nutrition services will be fully integrated to ensure effective two-way referrals between OPD, ANC/PNC, OTP/SC, and mental health services. To ensure quality and continuity of care, AYUUB will invest heavily in capacity building, training 50 frontline health and nutrition staff and supporting 10 community health workers (CHWs) to deliver community-based screening, counselling, follow-up, and referral. CHWs and Mother-to-Mother Support Groups will drive early detection of malnutrition, promote appropriate infant and young child feeding practices, and support defaulter tracing and service uptake at household level.ltbrgtNutrition interventions will combine treatment and prevention, including MUAC screening, OTP services, micronutrient supplementation, and caregiver counselling using the Kobciye Shurbad approach. Across all activities, the project will mainstream protection, gender, and accountability, ensuring inclusive, safe, and dignified access for women, persons with disabilities, IDPs, and minority groups. Strong coordination with the Ministry of Health, Health and Nutrition Clusters, UNICEF, WFP, WHO, and WASH and FSL partners will ensure convergence, avoid duplication, and maximize impact. Through this integrated, area-based approach, AYUUB will deliver timely, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian assistance aligned with SHF prioritiesltbrgtlt/pgt
